reefer-container.context: A side view of a shipping container with corrugated walls and a refrigeration unit with a fan at one end. Used for cold chain freight, temperature controlled cargo, food and pharma shipping and port logistics.

flat-rack-container.context: A container base with tall end walls and no sides, carrying a crate held down with a strap. Used for heavy lift, oversize and project cargo that will not fit in a closed box.

container-doors.context: The rear of a shipping container with two tall doors, each held shut by vertical locking bars. Used for container loading, door to door shipping, cargo security and seal checks.

container-truck.context: A semi truck cab pulling a chassis that carries a shipping container. Used for port haulage, intermodal transfers, drayage and container delivery tracking.

container-spreader.context: A crane spreader beam hung from a trolley by cables, with legs at each end that lock onto a container below. Used for port cranes, container terminals and lifting operations.

terminal-tractor.context: A short yard truck with a tall cab and a raised coupling plate on the rear deck. Used to shuttle trailers and containers around ports, depots and distribution yards.

swap-body.context: A truck box body standing on four folding steel legs with no truck underneath. Used for swap body transport, parcel hubs and trailer free storage, where bodies move between trucks and trains.

x-ray-cargo-scanner.context: An arched scanning gantry over a cargo truck, with beams passing down through the load. Used for customs inspection, border security and screening of freight without opening it.

container-yard.context: A top view of two long rows of stacked containers divided into bays, with a gantry bridge running across the top. Used for container terminals, storage yards and stacking plans.

well-car.context: A low railcar with a dropped centre well carrying two containers stacked on top of each other. Used for double stack rail freight, intermodal trains and container rail services.

gondola-railcar.context: An open-top railcar with ribbed sides and a heap of loose material above the rim. Used for bulk rail freight such as coal, scrap, aggregate and ore.

curtainsider-truck.context: A truck with a fabric curtain side shown as vertical folds, with a buckled strap along the lower edge. Used for curtain sided trailers, side loading freight and general haulage.

road-train.context: A truck cab pulling a long chain of three trailers. Used for long haul freight in remote regions, triple trailer combinations and high capacity road transport.

dry-bulk-trailer.context: A tanker trailer with a rounded tank and V shaped hopper cones hanging underneath. Used for powders and grain such as cement, flour and plastic pellets, unloaded from the bottom.

tail-lift-truck.context: A box truck with its lift platform lowered to the ground at the rear, carrying a box. Used for tail lift delivery, liftgate service and loading heavy items without a dock.

truck-mounted-forklift.context: A truck with a compact forklift carried on the back of its bed. Used for delivery without a dock, building material drops and off-loading at remote sites.

knuckle-boom-truck.context: A flatbed truck with a jointed crane arm folded behind the cab, lowering a crate. Used for loader crane trucks, site deliveries and self-unloading freight.

oversize-load.context: A truck carrying a load wider than itself, with a flag at each end of the load. Used for wide load warnings, abnormal load transport and heavy haulage permits.

tachograph.context: An in-dash recorder unit with a round dial, two display lines and a slot for the driver card. Used for driving hours records, speed recording and fleet compliance checks.

cargo-dolly.context: A flat roller platform on four small wheels with a tow bar. Used at airports to move cargo containers and pallets, and for baggage and air cargo ground handling.

handcart.context: A two-wheeled pushcart with a flat bed, a long handle and a pile of sacks on top. Used for market porters, hand hauling of goods and small scale transport.

reach-truck.context: A narrow electric lift truck with a tall mast, forks at the front and a stand-up operator cage. Used in narrow aisle racking, high bay warehouses and pallet put-away.

order-picker.context: A tall lift truck with the operator platform raised high beside a pallet shelf. Used for picking items from high racking and for man-up order picking in warehouses.

walkie-stacker.context: A pedestrian pallet stacker with a mast, raised forks carrying a pallet load and a long steering tiller. Used in small warehouses, shops and loading areas for lifting pallets on foot.

warehouse-robot.context: A squat, round-edged drive robot carrying a four-legged storage pod on its back. Used for goods to person picking, automated fulfilment centres and mobile robot fleets.

palletizing-robot.context: An industrial robot arm with a suction gripper setting a box onto a stack on a pallet. Used for end of line palletising, automated stacking and depalletising.

vertical-lift-module.context: A tall storage cabinet with a service window and a tray of parts pulled out at the front. Used for automated storage and retrieval of small parts, tools and spares in a small footprint.

carton-flow-rack.context: A side view of a shelf with sloped roller lanes, with cartons waiting at the low picking end. Used for gravity flow picking, first in first out stock and fast moving order picking.

cantilever-rack.context: A side view of a central upright column with long arms reaching out to both sides, each carrying pipes. Used for storing long items such as timber, pipes, tubes and bar stock.

warehouse-mezzanine.context: A raised steel platform on columns with a handrail above, and pallets stored underneath. Used for mezzanine floors, extra picking levels and making more use of warehouse height.

picking-cart.context: A wheeled cart with a push handle and two shelves holding labelled totes. Used for order picking rounds, batch picking and moving small items around a warehouse.

dock-leveler.context: A side view of a dock floor, a hinged steel plate sloping down to a trailer, and the trailer box above its wheel. Used for bridging the gap between a loading dock and a truck bed for forklifts.

dock-shelter.context: A front view of a loading door framed by thick padded curtains on three sides, with a roller door in the opening. Used for loading bays that seal against the back of a truck and keep out weather and draughts.

dock-bumper.context: A thick ribbed rubber block bolted to a wall plate. Used on loading docks to absorb the impact of reversing trucks and protect the building and trailers.

yard-ramp.context: A side view of a mobile steel ramp on wheels sloping up to the back of a trailer. Used for driving forklifts and pallet trucks into trailers and containers where there is no loading dock.

dock-plate.context: A top view of a rectangular metal plate with a diamond tread pattern and two slots for lifting handles. Used as a loose bridge between a dock and a truck bed, or as a ramp plate for wheeled loads.

ball-transfer-table.context: A top view of a square table covered in a grid of small balls, with a box resting on it. Used for moving boxes and parcels by hand in any direction at packing and sorting stations.

parcel-sorter.context: A top view of a conveyor line that splits into angled branches leading to chutes, with a box on the main belt. Used for parcel sortation, diverting items by destination and sort centres.

drum-truck.context: A two-wheeled hand truck with a curved cradle and a hook at the top holding a steel drum. Used for tilting and moving 200 litre drums and barrels by hand.

furniture-dolly.context: A low square platform with carpeted edges on casters, seen at three quarters. Used by movers to roll heavy furniture, pianos and appliances across floors.

stair-climbing-hand-truck.context: A hand truck with a three-wheeled triangular cluster at the bottom and a box strapped on. Used for carrying loads up and down stairs on delivery rounds and house moves.

pallet-wrapper.context: A turntable carrying a pallet load being wound with stretch film, with the film roll on a tall mast carriage. Used for securing loads before shipping and for stretch wrapping at the end of a packing line.

pallet-stack.context: A side view of five empty wooden pallets stacked on top of each other. Used for pallet storage, pallet returns, pallet exchange and pooling.

pallet-collar.context: A wooden pallet with two hinged wooden frames stacked on top, forming an open crate. Used for bulk transport and storage that can fold flat when empty.

cage-pallet.context: A steel wire mesh box on a pallet base, with a fold-down front panel. Used as a stackable storage cage, stillage and roll cage for loose or awkward goods.

pallet-box.context: A large corrugated box as wide as the pallet it sits on, with forklift openings visible below. Used for bulk shipping of loose goods and parts in a single pallet sized package.

octabin.context: A large eight-sided corrugated bulk box with a chamfered top, standing on a pallet. Used for shipping loose bulk items such as plastic pellets, food ingredients and small parts.

plastic-pallet.context: A top view of a molded plastic pallet with a ribbed grid deck and nine blocky feet. Used for hygienic, export and reusable pallets that do not splinter.

edge-protector.context: A box load with an angle strip fitted over its top corner. Used to protect cartons from strapping, to stiffen a stacked pallet load and to stop straps cutting in.

pallet-scale.context: A low weighing platform with a box on it and a digital readout on a post. Used to weigh pallets and freight for shipping costs, load limits and inventory checks.

spill-pallet.context: A grated platform sitting on a deep sump tray, with two upright drums standing on it. Used for spill containment when storing oil, paint and chemical drums.

strip-curtain.context: A doorway hung with vertical clear plastic strips, with one strip pushed aside. Used for cold room doors, freezer entrances and dock doors to keep in temperature and keep out dust and insects.

louvered-bin-rack.context: A wall panel with rows of horizontal louver slots, holding small open-front parts bins. Used for small parts storage in workshops, stockrooms and pick faces.

tote-dolly.context: A square wheeled base with four casters and a stack of plastic totes on top. Used to roll stacked totes and crates around a warehouse, store or kitchen without lifting.

collapsible-crate.context: A plastic crate with its walls folded flat into the base and one wall half raised. Used for reusable, foldable crates that save space on the return trip.

rfid-portal.context: A doorway gate with antenna posts on both sides and radio wave arcs over a pallet passing through. Used for reading RFID tags on pallets and cartons automatically at dock doors and gates.

rfid-reader.context: A handheld pistol-grip reader with a flat antenna paddle on top, sending out radio waves. Used for scanning RFID tags on stock, assets and parcels without line of sight.

ring-scanner.context: A barcode scanner worn on a finger with a strap, sending a scan beam toward a small barcode. Used for hands free scanning when picking, sorting and loading parcels.

voice-picking-headset.context: A single-ear headset with a boom microphone, next to a box on a shelf. Used for voice directed picking, where workers hear the next pick and confirm by speaking.

pick-to-light.context: A shelf front with two bins, one marked by a lit button and the other by a number display. Used for light directed picking, where a lit button shows the bin to take from and the quantity.

put-wall.context: A grid of open cubbies with some small parcels inside and indicator lights above the top row. Used for put wall sorting, where items are placed into slots by order for consolidation.

freight-elevator.context: A wide elevator car with vertical sliding gate bars and a loaded pallet inside. Used for moving pallets and goods between floors of warehouses, factories and stores.

mailer-box.context: A flat folded cardboard box with a hinged lid tucked into the front, the lid slightly raised. Used for e-commerce orders, subscription boxes and small item shipping.

poly-mailer.context: A flat plastic shipping bag with a peel strip flap at the top and a label on the front. Used for mailing clothing and soft goods that do not need a box.

paper-void-fill.context: An open box with crumpled kraft paper balls bulging out of the top. Used as packing paper to cushion items in a parcel and fill empty space.

packing-list-pouch.context: A clear adhesive envelope stuck on the face of a box, with a folded document visible inside. Used for holding packing slips, invoices and shipping paperwork on the outside of a parcel.

returnable-tote.context: A plastic tote box with a split lid folded shut and a hand hole at each end. Used for reusable transit totes that go back and forth between suppliers, stores and warehouses.

flexitank.context: A shipping container with its doors open, showing a bulging bladder filled with liquid. Used for shipping bulk liquids such as wine, oil and juice in a standard container.

stand-up-pouch.context: A flexible pouch standing upright on a gusseted base, with a zip line near the top. Used for food, snacks, coffee and liquids sold in resealable flexible packaging.

dry-ice.context: A stack of frosty ice cubes with curls of vapor rising off the top. Used for keeping parcels frozen in transit, cold chain shipping and warnings about dry ice packaging.

wardrobe-box.context: A tall moving box with the top open, showing a hanging rail with two clothes hangers. Used in removals to move clothes on hangers without folding them.

fiber-drum.context: A tall cylindrical cardboard drum with a metal lid clamped down by a locking ring. Used for shipping powders, granules and dry goods that need a sealed, light container.

honeycomb-paper.context: A sheet of kraft paper stretched into an open mesh of hexagon cells. Used as an eco friendly, recyclable wrap and cushioning for fragile items in place of bubble wrap.

foam-corner.context: A block of protective foam with a stepped notch cut out to cradle the corner of a box or frame. Used to protect the corners of furniture, glass panels and appliances in transit.

carton-divider.context: A top view of an open box split into a grid of cells by cardboard partitions, each cell holding a bottle. Used to keep glass bottles, jars and fragile items from touching in a shipping carton.

bottle-shipper.context: A molded pulp tray sleeve with bottle-shaped cavities, holding two bottles. Used to ship wine, beer and spirits safely in single or multi bottle packs.
